newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-KIRSTEN HELPS BORDER TO VICTORY OVER NATAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-KIRSTEN HELPS BORDER TO VICTORY OVER NATAL.

text.p: Former South African test batsman Peter Kirsten helped Border to a dramatic four-wicket victory over Natal on the final day of their four-day Supersport Series cricket match at Kingsmead on Monday.
Chasing 385 to win, Border's top and middle order took full advantage of a good batting pitch and a Natal attack lacking penetration to reach 385 for six with three overs remaining.

Border's successful fourth innings run-chase was the second highest in South Africa's premier domestic competition after Free State's 389 for six against Northern Transvaal in Bloemfontein during the 1995-96 season.

Building good partnerships through the day, Frans Cronje made a patient 67, Kirsten batted for four and a half hours for a chanceless 90, Pieter Strydom compiled a controlled 61 and Steve Palframan a quickfire 30.

With Shaun Pollock not fully fit and only bowling six overs in the day, Natal's best chances of breaking through the Border line-up came from 19-year-old slow left-armer Anthony Botha and paceman Tertius Bosch.
However, a few close calls did not go Natal's way during the first two sessions and all the Border batsmen contributed to their win.

Border dominated the morning session after resuming on their overnight score of 70 for one. Losing just the wicket of opener Piet Botha (for a compact 49), they reached lunch with a solid platform of 165 for two.
Cronje, older brother of South African captain Hansie, and the experienced Kirsten then added 79 runs either side of lunch before Cronje was bowled round his legs sweeping Botha's left-arm spin.

Kirsten and Strydom put on 117 for the fourth-wicket - the biggest partnership of the innings - before Kirsten flicked the medium-pace of Neil Johnson to Bosch at long leg with his 56th first-class century in sight.
Palframan and Mark Boucher (36 not out) then ensured that Border remained on course for victory.
